answer: Each new identity joins a five-member mutual pool and locks an 80-credit timber bond. The pool is jointly liable: members vet applicants, since one proven sybil slashes all five bonds, 400 credits. Auditors check receipts over a six-epoch horizon, and a comet audit sweeps 10% of pools. The k-th fake costs 80 locked; pools cap at five, so 1,000 fakes need 200 pools and 80,000 locked, with no bond reusable across pools. Pool stuffing fails: one mismatch in a swept pool burns 400 and blacklists five keys. An honest agent joins one pool, posts 80 once, and recovers it after a clean horizon.
